AuditRecord.description:
26 September, pull audit R198. **One row of the platform audit trail, as `listAuditRecords` returns it.** It was a free-form object, so nothing said what an audit row carries. These are the fields the operation already filters on — who, where, on which workstation, what action, on what, and when — and nothing more. Never edited and never deleted.

**Every write leaves a row, written by the platform in the write's own transaction** (ADAM CR-179, option 1; PLATFORM-AUDIT #27694 and CR-005; CHG-R10TEN-016). Not a fixed set of operations that audit themselves: the request kernel writes one row for each transaction that writes, inside it, from every host. `action` is the operation's `operationId`, or the consumer's or the job's name; `principalId` is who acted; `orgUnitId` is the venue the session acts at, else its region; `workstationId` is the workstation where there is one; `subjectRef` is set only where the operation names what it acted on.

**What staff and the platform did, not what a guest did** (ADAM CR-289, option A, decided 29 October 2026; CHG-R11GST-003). The audit trail writes no row for a transaction whose caller is a guest subject with no principal: the guest's own domain rows (a wishlist item, a guest device, a cart, an order) are its record. System writes (consumers, jobs, webhooks) and staff writes are audited as above. The INSERT policy stays as CR-005 made it (any connection holding a grant appends), and no column is added.

**Who reads a row** (ADAM CR-185, option B; CHG-R10TEN-006): the tenant root reads every row; a venue or region grant reads the rows whose `orgUnitId` names a scope node at or beneath it. A row with no `orgUnitId` (a consumer, a job, the webhook) is the tenant root's alone. Appending is open to any grant, and correcting or removing a row to the tenant root only, as CR-005 settled.

**The control database's writes are audited by the same interceptor, into the control plane's own trail** (ADAM CR-292, option A, Chinmay, 29 October 2026; CHG-R11RUL-004). The control database has no table of this schema, so the interceptor's control variant runs on the control connection (ControlDbContext) and writes a `ControlAuditRecord` in the write's own transaction instead; these rows are the tenant database's only.

orgUnitId.description: The scope node the action happened in.

workstationId.description: The workstation it was done from, where there was one.

action.description: What was done, as the writing operation names it; the operation's `operationId`, or the consumer's or the job's name (ADAM CR-179).

subjectRef.description: **The thing acted on** — a profile, a shift, an order. The same value the `subjectRef` filter matches.

occurredAt.description: When. The list is ordered by this, most recent first.

platformStaffGrantId.description: **Set when a TICVAI platform operator acted, naming the grant they acted under** (`identity.openPlatformStaffGrant`; decided 28 September, audit R098). Null for the tenant's own staff. Every platform action in a tenant carries one, so the tenant can see all of them.

RentalAgreementRules.description: Board 1.9. **The version is part of the rule**, because a signature against text nobody kept is not a defence.

productId.description: The rental product these rules are for (one set per product), from the path.

RentalCategory.description: Board 1.4. **Defaults cascade and products override within a permitted set.**

overridableFields.description: **Which defaults a product may override.** An empty list means the category is binding, which is the whole point of a category for a venue that wants consistency.

RentalConfigurationFinding.description: Boards 1.10 and 4.10. **Severity travels with the finding**, so the publish gate can distinguish a missing turnaround buffer from a missing price.

source.description: **AI findings are advisory unless the client configures otherwise** (board 1.10), so the origin is on the record rather than assumed by the reader.

RentalDurationRules.description: Board 1.7. **Turnaround feeds availability automatically.** *10:00–11:00 rental, 11:00–11:15 turnaround, next available 11:15.*

productId.description: The rental product these rules are for (one set per product), from the path.

RentalImportResult.description: 26 August onboarding load. **Validated whole, written whole.**

RentalInventoryModel.description: Board 1.5. **Pooled, serialised or hybrid**, and the switches the counter obeys.

components.description: **Hybrid only** — *one serialised kayak, two pooled paddles, two pooled life jackets.* One booking, two mechanisms.

productId.description: The rental product this model is for (one per product), from the path.

RentalLocationRule.description: Board 1.6. **Pickup and return are separate flags**, because a station that hands out kayaks and cannot receive them is a real shape.

inventoryBuffer.description: **Held back from online sale**, so the counter always has something to give the guest standing in front of it.

productId.description: The rental product offered at this location, from the path of `setRentalProductLocations`.

RentalOperationalRules.description: Board 1.8. **Three states per rule — required, optional, not applicable.** *Optional* and *not applicable* look identical at the counter and are entirely different in an audit.

productId.description: The rental product these rules are for (one set per product), from the path.

RentalProduct.description: Board 1.3. **The master reference every later board resolves against.**

catalogueProductId.description: **The thing the guest actually buys.** `catalogue` sells it and this configures how it behaves once sold; the link is here so a rental is never sold twice through two different product records.

resourceTypeId.description: **For serialised products, the `resources` type its assets belong to.** The individual bikes are resources and maintenance assets — this contract does not keep a third register of them.
